Subject: Post-call: Performance/SLO follow-up — p95/p99 latency targets (hosted API vs current provider)

Hi Samir — great to meet yesterday. Quick recap from our performance/SLO thread and a few follow-ups so we can scope a short evaluation: 

Key items we discussed (please confirm):
- Target end-to-end latency goals: p95 and p99 for your user flows (examples below).
- Typical concurrency and sustained throughput we should test for (RPS / concurrent sessions).
- Streaming/partial-result requirements (first-token latency vs per-token latency).
- Example prompts, average & max generation lengths, and any prompt templating that affects context window.

Can you confirm the exact p95/p99 targets you care about for the two primary flows: (1) short lookups (~<50 tokens) and (2) long responses (200+ tokens)? Also please attach any recent telemetry or benchmarks from your current provider — that will help us size tests and recommend hosted vs dedicated approach.

Suggested next steps: 
1) You send current provider p95/p99 numbers + representative prompt set and traffic profile.
2) We run a short perf eval (30–60 mins) against our hosted API in your region and share detailed breakdowns (p50/p95/p99, tail latencies by token, token throughput).
3) If you need contractual SLOs we can scope Dedicated capacity and the SLA implications.

If that works I can schedule a 30m performance deep-dive with our Sales Engineering and Infra teams for early next week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Attaching the telemetry we pulled last week. High-level from our side: 
- Short lookups (~<50 tokens): current provider p95 = 420ms, p99 = 1.1s (end-to-end).
- Long responses (~200+ tokens): p95 = 1.2s, p99 = 3.6s (higher tail when cache miss occurs).
- Sustained throughput: ~50 RPS observed during peak business hours; average concurrency ~10 simultaneous sessions.
- Streaming: yes — our UI expects incremental tokens and we consider first-token latency critical for perceived snappiness.

Notes: the current provider is running a mix of open models and a proprietary model; we see a lot of variability across regions. We've attached a CSV export of recent telemetry for the last 7 days. Happy to run a test on your hosted endpoint — would like to understand typical hosted-api p95/p99 you see for similar customers and whether Redwood will surface client-level tail metrics.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance/SLO follow-up — p95/p99 latency targets (hosted API vs current provider)

Thanks for the data, Samir — that telemetry is very helpful. A few clarifications and what you can expect from Redwood hosted API vs Dedicated: 
- Hosted API (typical, short-generation workloads): end-to-end p95 ~120–180ms, p99 ~300–500ms for our standard curated smaller models and optimized runtimes. These numbers assume short prompts (~<50 tokens) and single-request context.
- For longer generations or larger context windows those percentiles increase and depend on token output rate; typical first-token latency for streaming is in the ~60–100ms range, with incremental token latencies much lower.
- Tail spikes (p99) are often driven by µbursts of concurrency and cold KV-cache misses — we mitigate via prefix caching and continuous batching. If you need contract-level SLOs we usually recommend Dedicated to reduce cross-tenant variability and to guarantee capacity.

Proposed immediate plan:
1) We provision a short hosted evaluation endpoint in your preferred region and run a 60-minute load test matching your peak RPS and concurrency (we'll replay a subset of your telemetry).
2) We'll capture p50/p95/p99, first-byte latency for streaming, and per-token throughput.
3) Post-run we’ll deliver a perf report with recommendations (batching/quantization, model variant, Dedicated sizing) and an optional Dedicated trial if you want contractual SLOs.

If you can confirm region (US-west or US-east) and a 60-minute window next Wed/Thu, we'll book Sales Eng + Infra.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
